\noindent   \textit{Instructions: Answer   \textbf{five} questions including Question~1 which is compulsory. Symbols have their usual meanings.}
\bigskip

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 1.}

\begin{parts}
  \item What are the different types of scales of measurements? Explain each with a suitable example.
  \item Describe primary and secondary data. State their relative merits and defects.
  \item Explain different parts of a table.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 2.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Explain histogram, frequency polygon and ogives with examples and diagrams.
  \item Two sets of data consisting of $n_1$ and $n_2$ values have medians $M_1$, $M_2$ and means $ar{X}_1$ and $ar{X}_2$. Show that the combined median lies between $M_1$ and $M_2$, and the combined mean also lies between $ar{X}_1$ and $ar{X}_2$.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 3.}

\begin{parts}
  \item For discrete data, prove that the mean deviation is least when it is measured from the median.
  \item Prove that the mean deviation about the mean $ar{x}$ for a frequency distribution $(x_i, f_i; i=1, 2, \dots, n)$ is $\frac{2}{N}\sum_{x_i < ar{x}} f_i (ar{x} - x_i)$, where $N = \sum_{i=1}^n f_i$.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 4.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define raw and central moments. Define coefficients $eta_1, eta_2, \gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$. Prove that $eta_2 \ge 1$.
  \item When is a frequency distribution said to be a symmetrical distribution? Explain skewness and its different measures.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 5.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Give the axiomatic definition of probability. Using its axioms, prove that:
    
\begin{parts}
      \item $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$
      \item If $B \subset A$, then $P(B) \le P(A)$
    \end{parts}
  \item The chances of winning of two race horses are $a$ and $b$ respectively. What is the probability that at least one will win when the horses are running:
    
\begin{parts}
      \item in different races,
      \item in the same race.
    \end{parts}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 6.}

\begin{parts}
  \item A man alternately tosses a coin and throws a die, beginning with the coin. What is the probability that he will get a head before he gets a 5 or 6 on the die?
  \item An urn contains 6 white and 4 black balls, and a second urn contains 7 white and 2 black balls. A ball is randomly transferred from the first urn to the second urn, and then a ball is randomly transferred from the second urn back to the first urn. Now a ball is drawn from the first urn. What is the probability that it is white?
  \item The chances of A, B, and C becoming managers of a certain company are $4:2:3$. The probability that a bonus scheme will be introduced if A, B, or C becomes manager is $0.3$, $0.5$, and $0.8$ respectively. If the bonus has been introduced, what is the probability that A was appointed as the manager?
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 7.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define a random variable. A random variable $X$ has the following probability mass function:
    
\begin{center}
      
\begin{tabular}{c|cccc}
        $x$ & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
        \hline
        $f(x)$ & 0.1 & $K$ & $2K$ & 0.3
      \end{tabular}
    \end{center}
    
\begin{parts}
      \item Find the value of $K$, $E(X)$ and $V(X)$.
      \item Find the distribution function of $X$ and draw its graph.
    \end{parts}
  \item Define joint probability mass function (p.m.f.) of two discrete random variables. If the joint p.m.f. of $X_1$ and $X_2$ is:
    $$f(x_1, x_2) = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{21}, \quad x_1 = 1, 2, 3; \quad x_2 = 1, 2$$
    and $0$ otherwise. Find the marginal p.m.f. of $X_1$ and $X_2$, and the conditional p.m.f. of $X_1$ given $X_2 = 2$.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 8.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Two random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function:
    $$f(x, y) = \frac{1}{8}(6 - x - y), \quad 0 < x < 2, \quad 2 < y < 4$$
    and $0$ otherwise. Find:
    
\begin{parts}
      \item $P[X < 1  \text{ and } Y < 3]$
      \item $P[X + Y < 3]$
    \end{parts}
  \item If $(X, Y)$ has the joint p.d.f.:
    $$f(x, y) = kxy, \quad 0 < x < y < 1$$
    and $0$ otherwise. Find:
    
\begin{parts}
      \item the value of $k$,
      \item the marginal and conditional p.d.f.s.
    \end{parts}
\end{parts}
